subject: zoology_2
question_text: Describe the role of hypothalamus as a neuro-endocrine organ.

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book p.35, SAQ 26. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. Zoology-II holds only ONE source book in the corpus, so the two-book union check is structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is our reading of the question and is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Revised 2026-09-05 (examiner audit Z2-07): the s2 lines and mistake note now give the two routes separately, since the releasing and inhibiting hormones reach the anterior pituitary through the portal vessels while only oxytocin and vasopressin travel to the neurohypophysis.

steps.label: Where it lies
steps.why: It sits between the brain and the pituitary, which is exactly the position needed to turn nerve signals into hormone signals.
common_mistakes: Placing it above the thalamus. It lies below.
Leaving out its link to the pituitary.
steps.memory_tip: Below the thalamus, above the pituitary: the bridge between them.

steps.label: Neurosecretory cells
steps.why: These are nerve cells that release their product into the blood rather than onto another neuron, which is what makes the organ neuro-endocrine.
common_mistakes: Calling the nuclei glands. They are groups of nerve cells.
Sending the releasing hormones to the posterior lobe. They reach the anterior pituitary through the portal vessels.
steps.memory_tip: Nerve cells that secrete hormones: neurosecretory.
steps.margin_note: Name the nuclei and where their hormones go.
lines: It contains groups of neurosecretory cells

steps.label: Releasing and inhibiting hormones
steps.why: Having both a start signal and a stop signal lets the hypothalamus hold the pituitary at any level it needs.
common_mistakes: Naming only releasing hormones. Inhibiting hormones are equally marked.
Writing that the pituitary controls the hypothalamus. It is the other way round.
steps.memory_tip: One kind starts the pituitary, the other stops it.
steps.margin_note: Two named kinds, one line each.
lines: It secretes two kinds of hormones:

steps.label: Two named examples
steps.why: The same pituitary hormone has one hypothalamic hormone to switch it on and another to switch it off.
common_mistakes: Mixing the two up. Somatocrinin releases, somatostatin inhibits.
steps.memory_tip: Somatocrinin creates the signal; somatostatin stops it.
steps.margin_note: A pair of opposites makes the point clearly.

lines.text: Somatostatin stops the release of growth hormone

insider_note: Neuro-endocrine means it does two jobs. Say plainly that it is nerve tissue that makes hormones, or the point of the question is missed.
